solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Letters stolen by bitter evangelist

indicators.note: what is stolen is taken in and held, so the letters go inside the beer

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, ale
letters as in mail, the post

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a resentful preacher has been pinching their mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like an adjective for the evangelist, but it is a noun: bitter is a hoppy British beer. 'stolen by' signals the mail going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve apostles spread the gospel, so an evangelist or missionary preacher is one.

clue.text: Bold leader in historic Scottish city

parts.note: bold, cheeky, impudent: pert

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of historic

explanation.surface: A daring chief within an old Scottish town's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historic' seems to describe the city but only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is a city on the River Tay in central Scotland, once its capital.

clue.text: Motorbike attachment that's hurried, is the wrong way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, being the wrong way up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: hurried means raced

explanation.surface: A sidecar fitted to a speeding motorbike has ended up upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way up' signals reading upwards, which suits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is the small passenger car bolted to the side of a motorcycle.

clue.text: Search briefly for toilet

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to search is to look

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick look around for a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' seems to describe the search but docks the last letter of LOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is the everyday British word for a lavatory or WC.

clue.text: Wrong, a girl

parts.note: a girl or young woman is a miss

explanation.surface: A curt remark that someone is mistaken, addressed to a young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is faulty or not right, as in 'something is amiss'.

clue.text: God a degree above king and queen!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece above another comes before it

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: An exclamation that God ranks one level higher than any king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: God is called the Maker as the creator of everything.

clue.text: Odd way to introduce series

indicators.note: the first piece comes in front of, introducing, the second

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way
a range is a series, as of products

explanation.surface: An unusual method for launching a television series.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and strange are synonyms meaning peculiar or unusual.

clue.text: Bloomer getting daughter into other dodgy card game

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is put into the reshuffled word
dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters of other are rearranged

parts.note: poker is a card game

explanation.surface: A blunder in which a daughter is lured into a shady game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder but means a flowering plant. 'dodgy' rearranges OTHER to REHOT, and 'into' puts D inside it to make REDHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-hot poker, or kniphofia, is a garden plant with tall spikes of flame-coloured flowers.

clue.text: Person throwing jug

definitions.meaning: in baseball, the player throwing the ball to the batter
a large jug for pouring liquids

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a baseball's thrower and a large vessel for water or milk.

clue.text: A little peach, occasionally sweet

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fruit now and then, with a bit of something sugary on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' looks like an alternate-letter signal but is just part of the text holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc is informal British shorthand for chocolate, a sweet or confection.

clue.text: Changing, triangle shatters

indicators.note: a triangle that shatters breaks into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A percussion triangle breaks apart as it is being swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering means modifying or changing something.

clue.text: Versus a profit, loss finally beginning to tell

parts.note: a profit is a gain

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of loss
the beginning of tell is its first letter

explanation.surface: Profit pitted against loss, which eventually starts to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profit' and 'loss' look like a contrasted pair, but loss only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus and against both mean in opposition to, as in a contest.

clue.text: Ancient city, portion in South Africa

indicators.note: the portion is placed in the abbreviation for South Africa

parts.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: A sliver of ancient history found somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a warlike city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Road hazard, this half visible in Dorset town

indicators.note: the half word is seen inside the town's name

parts.note: Poole is a harbour town in Dorset, a county in southern England

indicators.note: half of this is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A warning that this road danger is partly visible in a Dorset town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county on England's south coast, and its harbour town Poole is the container; 'visible in' and 'half' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface that endangers vehicles.

clue.text: Loathing crimson fez, perhaps?

parts.note: a fez is an example of a hat
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Someone hating a scarlet fez.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written hat then red, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing and hatred both name intense dislike.

clue.text: A royal primarily in woven satin, Russian empress

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes in the woven word
woven threads are interlaced, so the letters of satin are rearranged
primarily takes the first letter of royal

explanation.surface: A royal wearing woven satin is the Russian empress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges SATIN to TSINA, and 'in' puts AR (A plus R from 'primarily' royal) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a female ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Cook retains right sieve

indicators.note: to cook is to fiddle or tamper with, so the letters of retains are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef keeps the correct kitchen sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a kitchen person but signals rearranging, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or mesh utensil used to drain liquids.

clue.text: Stage player originally cast to appear in upcoming schedule

indicators.note: the letter appears in the middle of the reversed schedule
in a down clue upcoming means rising, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of cast

explanation.surface: A performer cast at the start appears in the coming programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns ROTA into ATOR, and 'to appear in' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a performer who plays a part on stage.

clue.text: Card carrying first of nine spots

indicators.note: the card carries, holds, the letter within it

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

indicators.note: first of takes the first letter of nine

explanation.surface: A playing card with the first of nine pips on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like a card's pips but means pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, i.e. spots.

clue.text: Darkness close, end of daylight

parts.note: close means near, nigh

indicators.note: the end of daylight is its last letter

explanation.surface: Darkness draws near as daylight ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark time between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Still owed? Wonderful!

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unpaid debt and something excellent that stands out.

clue.text: Catch tail-enders in Australian side, distraught

indicators.note: tail-enders are a cricket team's last batsmen, so this takes each word's last letter

explanation.surface: Taking catches off the lower order in a struggling Australian cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: Tail-enders are cricket's weakest batsmen, who bat last; here they are the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it, as with a fishing net.

clue.text: Long twelve months before end of recession

parts.note: twelve months make a year

indicators.note: the end of recession is its last letter

explanation.surface: A long year waiting for a recession to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is a verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn, desire it.

clue.text: The last reshuffles in secrecy

indicators.note: reshuffles means the letters are mixed up again

explanation.surface: A final cabinet reshuffle conducted on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is a covert, secret manner of acting.
